text:
incident-bot: ALERT — Canary rollout for service runtime-proxy showing error-rate spike. Metric: 5xx rate 9.8% (canary), stable 0.2% — triggered at 2025-11-14T09:12:47Z (thread start).
marta (oncall): I'm on it. seeing the same in grafana. p95 latency up ~450ms for canary. Canary tranche is ~3% traffic.
devin (eng-infra): tagging in here — recent CI built image: registry.redwood.internal/runtime-proxy:canary-20251114-88a1
raj (releases): that image should have been identical to stable sha abc1234 but the digest differs. CI reported successful push but no signing step executed.
sylvia (support): customer-impact: a handful of API customers (prod keys) reported 502s starting ~09:11. ETA on rollback? customers asking.
marta (oncall): can we cut traffic to canary and scale it to zero? If it's an image/regression better to rollback immediate.
deploy-bot: deploy pipeline event: canary rollout initiated by raj@releases at 2025-11-14T09:08:12Z — 6 pods scheduled.
chris (sre): quick check: kube events show image pull succeeded but container restarted frequently with OOMKilled logs and repeated startup panic logs referencing plugin loader. suspect a corrupted layer or wrong build variant.
devin (eng-infra): digging into registry: found retag event — mirror job retagged digest sha256:deadbeef -> tag canary-20251114 after mirror sync. looks like cross-arch retag from a stale mirror. this is suspicious for cache-poisoning.
raj (releases): our CI used a mutable tag during the mirror push step. Ugh — pipeline allowed push with same tag twice. I'm disabling the mirror job now and starting an immutable push workflow.
marta (oncall): steps: 1) reduce canary traffic to 0, 2) scale canary deployment replicas=0, 3) restore stable by forcing image to stable digest, 4) toggle feature flag as kill-switch if deploy changes required. I'll run 1-2.
marta (oncall): kubectl -n prod scale deploy runtime-proxy-canary --replicas=0
ops-bot: Command acknowledged. Scaled deployment "runtime-proxy-canary" to 0 replicas.
deploy-bot: rollback initiated by marta (oncall). Target image: registry.redwood.internal/runtime-proxy@sha256:abc1234-stable
raj (releases): pushing rollback to kube: `kubectl set image deployment/runtime-proxy runtime=registry.redwood.internal/runtime-proxy@sha256:abc1234-stable -n prod`
chris (sre): rolling update started. watching pods... stable pods re-serving traffic. p95 latency returning to baseline within expected ramp.
sylvia (support): noting customers: 6 incidents created, support on it. I'll send short comms that we saw degraded canary and rolled back, investigating root cause.
devin (eng-infra): digging logs from registry: mirror relayer retried an old blob upload after timeout causing tag to point to older incompatible layer. Also saw registry returning 202 during push then later 200 for same tag — race condition.
marta (oncall): recommended mitigation: block mirror job for mutable tags, enforce digest pinning in release pipeline, add registry push signing step.
raj (releases): immediate mitigation: change pipeline to push with immutable tag (build-<gitshort>-<ts>) and update release automation to reference digests. I'll open PR now.
chris (sre): feature-flag kill-switch ready as last resort: `flags toggle runtime_proxy_v2 --off --actor marta` — not used because rollback sufficed, but availability for future incidents.
marta (oncall): confirming customer-facing impact: partial (6 customers) with transient 502s; no data loss, all back to normal.
ops-bot: incident ticket created: INC-20251114-1287 (canary-image-retag-cache-poison). Assigning to releases + eng-infra for postmortem.
devin (eng-infra): immediate follow-ups: 1) add registry push verification (digest check), 2) prevent mirror from retagging existing tags, 3) add alert for unexpected digest mismatch between CI manifest and registry returned digest.
raj (releases): PR opened: enforce immutable tags + digest pinning in pipelines — link: https://git.internal/redwood/releases/pull/412
sylvia (support): I'll prepare a short customer note and coordinate with CSMs for impacted accounts.
marta (oncall): handing off to chris for remainder of incident review and postmortem action items. I'm secondary oncall next shift if needed.
chris (sre): acknowledged handoff. I'll drive the postmortem and make sure action items land. thx all. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: RESOLVED — Canary traffic 0, rollback complete, error rate back to baseline. Thread closed at 2025-11-14T09:23:40Z (last message).
